title: ‘आगोको फिलुङ्गो’ कथामा प्रतिनिधित्व, पहिचान र प्रतिरोध
nepali: प्रस्तुत शोधलेख विजय चालिसेद्वारा लेखिएको ‘आगोको फिलुङ्गो’ कथामा चित्रित प्रतिनिधित्व, पहिचान र प्रतिरोधका दृष्टिले सीमान्तकृत समुदायको अध्ययनसँग सम्बद्ध छ । यसमा सीमान्तकृत समुदायप्रति प्रभुत्वशाली वर्गको शोषण र उत्पीडनको अध्ययन साथै वर्गीय, लैङ्गिक प्रतिनिधित्व र पहिचान, सांस्कृतिक वर्चस्व र प्रतिरोध, अर्थको उत्पादन र ग्रहणको प्रक्रियाका अवस्था केकस्तो रहेको छ भन्ने जिज्ञासाको समाधान खोज्ने प्रयत्न गरिएको छ । यसका लागि सांस्कृतिक अध्ययन सम्प्रदायका स्टेवार्ड हलको अर्थको उत्पादन र ग्रहण सम्बन्धी मान्यतालाई कृति विश्लेषणको मुख्य आधार बनाइएको छ । अध्ययनका क्रममा ‘आगोको फिलुङ्गो’ कथाले नेपाली समाजमा राज्य सताद्वारा सीमान्तमा पारिएका समुदायलाई दमनकारी उपकरणका माध्यमबाट दमन र उत्पीडनमा पारेको प्रसङ्लाई जोडदार रूपमा उठाएको र सीमान्तकृत वर्गले आफूहरूमाथि गरिएको दमन र उत्पीडनका विरुद्ध सशक्त प्रतिरोध गरेको यथार्थलाई महत्त्वका साथ प्रस्तुत गरेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: The present research article is concerned with the study of marginalized communities in terms of representation, identity, and resistance depicted in the short story 'Aagoko Philungo' ('Spark of Fire') written by Bijay Chalise. In this, an attempt has been made to examine the exploitation and oppression of marginalized communities by the dominant class, as well as to seek solutions to questions regarding the conditions of class and gender representation and identity, cultural hegemony and resistance, and the processes of encoding and decoding of meaning. For this purpose, the perspective on the production and reception of meaning by Stuart Hall of the cultural studies tradition has been adopted as the primary basis for analyzing the work. In the course of the study, the conclusion is drawn that the story 'Aagoko Philungo' forcefully raises the issue of communities pushed to the margins by the state power in Nepali society being subjected to repression and oppression through repressive apparatuses, and prominently presents the reality that the marginalized class mounted robust resistance against the repression and oppression inflicted upon them.

informal_english: This research article looks into marginalized communities through the lens of representation, identity, and resistance depicted in Bijay Chalise's short story 'Aagoko Philungo' ('Spark of Fire'). In this, an attempt is made to examine how the dominant class exploits and oppresses marginalized communities, while seeking answers about class and gender representation and identity, cultural hegemony and resistance, and how meaning is produced and received. To do this, Stuart Hall's cultural studies perspective on the encoding and decoding of meaning has been used as the main foundation for analyzing the work. Over the course of the study, the conclusion is drawn that the story 'Aagoko Philungo' forcefully brings up how communities pushed to the margins by state power in Nepali society get subjected to repression and oppression through repressive apparatuses, and prominently highlights the reality that the marginalized class mounted solid resistance against the repression and oppression inflicted upon them, eh.
